sessions.situation: A project, launch, or incident produced results the group needs to learn from.

sessions.title: Reset After Change
sessions.situation: A reorganization, layoff, leadership change, or similar shift has left people uncertain.
sessions.output: A filled Who We Are Now canvas: built live on the board, no drafting afterward: with four zones: - What continues: what is not changing. Gives people solid ground. - What's ending: what we're letting go of. Naming it once stops months of relitigating it. - From → To: 3–5 shifts, “We were ___ → we are now ___,” each marked *true now* or *not yet true*. People know how to act today, and nobody pretends the change is further along than it is. - Open questions: each answered now, given an answer date and owner (“I'll confirm by…”), or marked “can't share yet.” Uncertainty becomes owned and scheduled. Test: afterward, anyone in the room can explain what changed, what didn't, how to act now, and what they're still waiting on and when: the same way their colleagues would. The anonymous pulse is a readout for leaders, not part of the canvas.

sequence.setting: What changed, why, and what's decided versus still open. The leader gives it if present; otherwise Joe reads the announced change.
Anonymous: how are you feeling about the change? A readout for leaders.
Who We Are Now canvas: everyone writes into Continuing · Ending · New, then pairs endings with what's new into “We were ___ → we are now ___.”
The 3–5 From → To shifts that matter most; mark each true now or not yet true.
Check: “who we are now,” in one line each.
Anonymous: worries and questions, into the open-questions zone.
Answer now · answer by a date · can't share yet. Joe proposes the sort; the leader confirms.
The leader answers the “answer now” questions, 60 seconds each.
Owners and answer-by dates on the canvas, plus a date to pulse again.

techniques.do: Ask one short question; the right person, or anyone, answers in one line; capture it and move on · Joe: 1 min · conventional: 5–10 min of open discussion.

techniques.name: Timed Turns
techniques.purpose: let people speak without creating an open floor
techniques.do: Define order and 30–60 seconds per person; signal at time and move immediately · Joe: 3 min · conventional: 15–20 min.

techniques.name: Buzzer
techniques.purpose: stop a speech without stopping the room
techniques.do: Announce it at the start. Use it whenever someone starts making a speech or runs past their turn, then redirect at once: usually into Convert, Don't Debate.
techniques.say: “I'm going to use a buzzer. If you start a speech, you'll hear it. It's rude to one person and kind to the whole group.”

techniques.name: Time Signals
techniques.do: Give a 30-second warning, call time, and move immediately. Slower writers keep writing and add later.
techniques.say: “Thirty seconds.” · “Time. If you're mid-sentence, finish it: you can always add more later.”

techniques.name: Questions in Chat
techniques.do: Ask for questions in chat. Watch it while people produce; answer privately or restate the instruction to the whole room.
techniques.say: “Everybody will get more if you don't ask the question you have. Put it in the chat: just play along and you'll get it.”

techniques.name: Audible
techniques.purpose: change the plan when the room stalls
techniques.do: Treat a visible stall as a design signal. Stop, then change the play or what comes next. Spend the session's slack (plans finish about 10 minutes early); if time remains at the end, add a quick extra play.

techniques.name: Parking Lot
techniques.purpose: keep concerns heard without derailing the flow
techniques.do: Park off-pace items visibly. Name parked items in the last 10–15 minutes; they live in the post-session write-up. Foundation items may be parked only when the session agreement says to push through, and are labeled as foundation issues.
techniques.say: “Let's put that in the parking lot.” · “These are the things in the parking lot for you.”

techniques.name: Convert, Don't Debate
techniques.purpose: turn one person's objection into everyone's production
techniques.do: Buzz, park the point, then run a 1-minute all-hands writing audible on it. For “not safe to try”: 1 minute to write reasons, 1 minute to read and add red stickies, then noted dissent if the decider does not decide.
techniques.say: “Let's park that. Quick audible: everybody has one minute to write the reasons this might not be safe to try.”

techniques.name: Lightning Briefing
techniques.purpose: bring needed facts into the room without pre-work
techniques.do: One person who knows the facts gives a strict 3-minute input. Everyone else writes questions in chat. It builds on the session pre-brief and never assumes it was read.
techniques.say: “Three minutes, then I'll buzz. Questions go in the chat.”

techniques.name: Threshold Line
techniques.purpose: turn scores into a decision boundary fast
techniques.do: Show the scored list in rank order. Point to the natural break in the scores and ask the decider to set the line. Everything above it is in; everything below is sorted afterward.
techniques.say: “Here's the ranked list. Where's the natural break? [Decider], draw the line.”

techniques.name: Blameless Frame
techniques.purpose: make it safe to say what really happened
techniques.do: Open the retro or review with one line that sets the frame, then hold it whenever talk drifts toward blame. Blameless about the past; accountable for the improvement.
techniques.say: “Everyone did the best they could with what they knew at the time. We're here to fix conditions, not judge people.”
